knowledge-base.overview: Ktor 2.x / Kotlin 1.9+ guardrails, patterns, and best practices for lightweight microservices and REST APIs. Leverages Kotlin coroutines natively. Covers modular plugin architecture (Serialization, Authentication, StatusPages, RequestValidation, Routing), type-safe routing DSL as Route extension functions, JWT authentication, Exposed ORM with HikariCP, centralized error handling, testApplication integration tests, and MockK unit tests. Loaded automatically when agents work on Ktor-based .kt files.

core-principles.principle: Configure behavior via installable plugins in separate files under plugins/. Never put plugin installs inside route blocks.
All request handling is suspend. Never block the event loop with synchronous I/O.
Use Kotlin's type system for routing, configuration, and serialization (kotlinx.serialization, not Jackson/Gson).
Wire services via constructor parameters. No global singletons or GlobalScope usage.
Use application.conf with ${?ENV_VAR} overrides. Never hardcode secrets.

guardrail.rule: Never block the event loop with synchronous I/O. Always use withContext(Dispatchers.IO) for blocking calls.
Never use GlobalScope for request-scoped work. Use the request's coroutine scope.
Never install plugins inside route blocks. All plugin installation must be in Application.module() via configure* functions.
Never expose internal exception messages to API clients. Always use StatusPages to map to structured error responses.
guardrail.good: exception<Throwable> { call, cause -> call.application.environment.log.error("Unhandled exception", cause) call.respond(HttpStatusCode.InternalServerError, ErrorResponse(500, "INTERNAL_ERROR", "An unexpected error occurred")) }

guardrail.rule: Skip request validation on no user-facing endpoint. Install RequestValidation and validate all request DTOs before service calls.
Use kotlinx.serialization for JSON. Never use Jackson or Gson with Ktor unless explicitly required.
Handle CancellationException correctly: rethrow it, never swallow it.
Use newSuspendedTransaction for all Exposed ORM calls. Raw transactions block the coroutine dispatcher.
Define routes as Route extension functions in routes/, not inline in configureRouting().
Never hardcode configuration values. Use application.conf with ${?ENV_VAR} overrides.
Use supervisorScope when child coroutine failures should not cancel siblings.
Use withTimeout for external service calls to prevent unbounded waiting.

knowledge-base.project-structure:
myapp/ ├── src/main/kotlin/com/example/ │ ├── Application.kt # Entry point, module composition │ ├── plugins/ # One file per plugin │ │ ├── Routing.kt │ │ ├── Serialization.kt │ │ ├── Security.kt │ │ ├── StatusPages.kt │ │ ├── Validation.kt │ │ └── Databases.kt │ ├── routes/ # Route extension functions │ │ ├── UserRoutes.kt │ │ └── AuthRoutes.kt │ ├── models/ # Data models, DTOs, Exposed table objects │ │ ├── User.kt │ │ └── Requests.kt │ ├── services/ # Business logic (suspend functions) │ │ └── UserService.kt │ ├── repositories/ # Data access (Exposed, suspend) │ │ └── UserRepository.kt │ └── utils/ │ └── JwtUtils.kt ├── src/main/resources/ │ ├── application.conf # HOCON configuration │ └── logback.xml ├── src/test/kotlin/com/example/ │ ├── ApplicationTest.kt # testApplication integration tests │ └── services/UserServiceTest.kt # MockK unit tests ├── build.gradle.kts └── gradle.properties
Conventions: - plugins/ One configure* extension per file - routes/ Route extension functions injecting services - services/ Suspend business logic; throws domain exceptions - repositories/ Suspend; wraps all DB access in newSuspendedTransaction

pattern.name: Module Composition (Application.kt)
pattern.description: Install plugins in dependency order. Serialization before Routing; StatusPages early.
pattern.example: fun Application.module() { configureSerialization() // ContentNegotiation first configureValidation() // RequestValidation before routing configureSecurity() // Authentication before protected routes configureStatusPages() // Error handling catches all configureDatabases() // Database connection pool configureRouting() // Routes last (depends on all above) }
